title: CFPB Data: 63% of 'Pay in 4' Users Stack Multiple Loans
alt_title_1: What 53.6 Million Buy Now, Pay Later Accounts Actually Show
alt_title_2: Why 'Zero Interest' Pay-in-4 Splits Turn Into Stacked Debt
description_hook: Federal reports from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau tracking six major Buy Now, Pay Later lenders show 53.6 million users taking an average of 6.3 loans per year, with 62.7% holding simultaneous BNPL loans in credit-panel data.

scenes.headline: 62.7% Held Overlapping Loans
scenes.narration: Why do 63 percent of Buy Now, Pay Later borrowers hold overlapping loans at once?
scenes.source: CFPB Consumer Use of BNPL Report Table 4 (Jan 2025)

scenes.headline: 53.6 Million Pay-in-4 Borrowers
scenes.narration: Across six major lenders tracked by the CFPB, 53.6 million borrowers averaged 6.3 loans per year.

scenes.headline: Holiday Auto-Debits Collide
scenes.narration: Federal data shows active split plans spiking every holiday week, creating overlapping biweekly bank drafts.

scenes.headline: Higher Unsecured Debt Loads
scenes.narration: BNPL users also carried heavier card and personal debt, though the CFPB stresses correlation is not causation.

scenes.headline: One Split Loan at a Time
scenes.narration: Zero interest is still real debt. Pay one Pay-in-4 plan to zero before opening another.
